paragraphs: Children in care from Gateshead live with the council's own foster carers or with independent agencies such as the services shown above. Gateshead Council describes its fostering service as the most direct route to caring for the borough's looked-after children, and says Ofsted rated it Good in 2024. It looks for short-term, long-term and respite carers: some children go home after days or weeks, while others stay for several years or until they are grown up.

The council's information on teenagers explains that the teenage years are a critical stage for young people who have had a difficult start, and it asks for carers with patience and a willingness to learn. To enquire you need to be over 21, have a spare room and, on the council's own campaign page, live within about 20 miles of Gateshead.

Gateshead also runs a role it calls Community Foster Care, where approved carers spend at least two days a week helping families stay together and supporting kinship and other foster families, paid for their contracted hours. Its first Mockingbird constellation links a hub carer with six to ten nearby fostering households for advice, social time and sleepovers.

Council carers get a named supervising social worker who usually visits monthly, out-of-hours telephone support every day of the year, support groups, respite, therapeutic and education support, and independent advice through FosterTalk. Training runs on evenings, weekends and online, and some of it counts towards a skills payment on top of a graded child allowance. Gateshead is one of twelve councils in Foster with North East, the regional hub that handles first enquiries.
Before deciding, speak to the council and two or three of the services listed here, and ask each what it pays, how it trains new carers and who you would call at night.

sources.title: It's never been a better time to foster with Gateshead (Gateshead Council)
